analysis:
The only change in this PR is test-only, in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Tools/FlintNativeProtocolTests.swift. It adds maskCacheKeysIdentifyIdenticalMasksAndOptIntoChaining (head lines 209-226) and one assertion in statePoolExhaustionIsBoundedAndCannotBecomeNormalEOS (head line 267). Neither touches production code, the coordinator-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009) or App Attest authorization (TB-011). The tests exercise FlintNativeProtocolConstraint APIs (maskCacheKey, allowsChainedDecode) that are not supplied here, so they imply a production change elsewhere in the PR. That change is outside this batch. A mask cache keyed by (state, remainingTokens) and the opt-in to chained decode could affect tool-call constraint enforcement (the protocol-level guard against reasoning text executing quoted tool calls, and the fail-closed behavior on state-pool exhaustion).

The new tests assert the properties that matter. Equal cache keys must imply identical masks. A nil key must be returned for remaining=0, for out-of-range states and for an exhausted state pool. Together these show that a key collision cannot widen the allowed-token mask and that exhaustion fails closed, with no normal EOS.

A next pass should check the production implementation for three things. First, the key must encode everything that affects the mask: the mode, the tool set, the parallel-call allowance and the remaining-token budget, including the boundary between remaining=1 and remaining=2. Second, the cache must be per-request or per-constraint, so that no cross-request or cross-tenant state is shared (T-041-style leakage). Third, the chained decode must not bypass per-step constraint masking. No security regression is identified in the supplied test-only diff.
